title: Choose Listings with Minimum Count Then Capacity
prompt:
Implement `select_group_listings(listings, group_size, neighborhood) -> list[str]`. Each listing is a mapping with a unique string `id`, a `neighborhood`, and a nonnegative integer `capacity`. Consider only listings whose neighborhood equals the requested `neighborhood`. Return the IDs of a subset whose total capacity is at least `group_size`.

Rank feasible subsets by `(listing_count, total_capacity, original_index_tuple)`: first minimize the number of selected listings, then minimize their combined capacity, then use original input positions only as a deterministic final tie-breaker. Return the selected IDs in original input order. Return `[]` when no eligible subset is feasible. Assume all inputs satisfy the stated shape. Do not mutate the input. This is a practice reconstruction of a reported Airbnb prompt; the tie-break makes its stated two-level objective executable.

example.reasoning: One listing is preferred to two even though its total capacity is higher; listing count is the primary objective.
